item.title: Dollarama to only pass on price increases from war where 'absolutely necessary': CEO
item.description: As conflict in the Middle East drives up the cost of many daily essentials, the head of Dollarama Inc. says the company will try to resist hiking its own prices as much as possible.

item.title: New York plane crash investigation looking at cockpit recorder and controllers
item.description: NEW YORK (AP) — Investigators looking into the collision between an Air Canada jet and a fire truck at New York’s LaGuardia Airport are reviewing the cockpit voice recorder and what was happening inside the control tower moments before the crash.

item.title: Liberals to debate age restrictions on social media, AI chatbots
item.description: OTTAWA — Age restrictions on using social media accounts and AI chatbots are among the topics up for debate when Liberal party grassroots gather next month for their national convention.

item.title: Fire out and shelter-in-place order is lifted after oil refinery explosion near Texas coast
item.description: An oil refinery fire near the Texas coast was put out Tuesday and a shelter-in-place order was lifted, hours after a large explosion at the complex shot plumes of smoke into the air, officials said.

item.title: Pride festivals seek federal $3M as corporations pull back support amid DEI backlash
item.description: OTTAWA — Pride festivals are seeking $3 million annually from Ottawa to fill a funding gap left by organizers pulling back funding amid a backlash to diversity, equity and inclusion programs.

item.title: Canadian sport system 'broken, unsustainable,' federal commission finds
item.description: Canadian sport needs an overhaul. That's the conclusion of the Future of Sport in Canada Commission's final report released Tuesday.

item.title: Five things about the Future of Sport in Canada Commission
item.description: What is the Future of Sport in Canada Commission? Announced in December, 2023 by former federal sports minister Carla Qualtrough, the commission was among various federal government remedies in response to a wave of maltreatment and abuse reports,

item.title: Air Canada crash probe being conducted in 'full co-operation' with U.S.: Carney
item.description: OTTAWA — Prime Minister Mark Carney says Ottawa is working in "full co-operation" with officials in the United States to probe the crash of an Air Canada jet at New York's LaGuardia Airport that killed two pilots Sunday night.

item.title: Global Affairs laying off its most skilled diplomats, union says
item.description: OTTAWA — The union representing staff at Global Affairs Canada says the foreign service is laying off dozens of its most skilled diplomats, while asking other envoys moving across continents to wait months for their personal items.

item.title: Vegas and Seattle a step closer to getting NBA teams. League's owners approve expansion exploration
item.description: NEW YORK (AP) — Seattle and Las Vegas are one step closer to having NBA teams.

item.title: B.C. Grade 6 teacher disciplined after dry ice 'explosion' in class
item.description: A middle school teacher in southeastern British Columbia has agreed to a two-day suspension of his teaching certificate after he brought dry ice to class, leading to the "explosion" of a water bottle that frightened some students.

item.title: Supreme Court sides with Cox Communications in a copyright fight with record labels over downloads
item.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Supreme Court on Wednesday sided with internet service provider Cox Communications in its copyright fight with record labels over illegal music downloads by Cox customers.

item.title: Canada is not planning to reopen embassy in Syria
item.description: OTTAWA — The federal government says it has no plans to reopen its embassy in Syria.

item.title: Three heli-skiers killed in northwest B.C. avalanche were Swiss nationals: consulate
item.description: A Swiss government official has confirmed the three people who died in an avalanche in northwestern British Columbia on Sunday were Swiss nationals.

item.title: Quebec Conservatives nab their only legislature seat with ex-CAQ member joining party
item.description: QUÉBEC — The Quebec Conservatives now have an elected member in the national assembly after a former cabinet minister with the Coalition Avenir Québec crossed the floor to join the party.
